summary: Anthropic 2027 exit ARR will be $400-500B, above Wall Street consensus by 25-30%
summary_extended: Baker argues that Anthropic's 2027 exit ARR will land in the $400–500B range, which he estimates is 25–30% above prevailing Wall Street consensus for the company. He frames this as a deliberate directional bet on the 'over,' grounded in his view that demand for Anthropic's frontier AI services is not the binding constraint — rather, physical compute capacity and energy availability are the primary limiters on how fast revenue can scale. The implication is that if those infrastructure constraints are relieved (through new datacenter builds, power agreements, or chip supply), Anthropic's revenue trajectory could surprise significantly to the upside. Baker's thesis is forward-looking into a pre-IPO company, making it an actionable view primarily for private market investors or those positioning around Anthropic's anticipated IPO, which the episode context suggests could occur around 2027.
detail: Baker takes the over on whatever Wall Street consensus is for Anthropic 2027 revenue by 25-30%. He frames $400-500B exit ARR as 'within the zone of realistic and achievable,' constrained primarily by physical compute/energy limits rather than demand.
confidence_evidence: Baker makes an explicit directional bet on the over vs. consensus, gives a specific range, and explains the constraint thesis in detail
